verses.1: Joseph was taken down to Egypt and sold there by the Ishmaelites to Potiphar, an Egyptian official who was Pharaoh's cupbearer.
verses.2: The LORD was with Joseph, so that he became a successful man. He was in the household of his Egyptian master,
verses.3: and his master saw that the LORD was with him and that the LORD made everything he did prosper.
verses.4: Joseph found favor in his eyes, and he made him a servant in his household. Potiphar put him in charge of his house and gave him everything he owned into his hand.
verses.5: From the time he put him in charge of his house and all his property, the LORD blessed the Egyptian's household for Joseph's sake. The blessing of the LORD was upon everything he had in the house and in the field.
verses.6: Potiphar left everything he had in Joseph's charge and did not concern himself with anything except the food he ate. Now Joseph was handsome in appearance and pleasing in form.
verses.7: After these events, his master's wife set her eyes on Joseph and said, "Lie with me."
verses.8: But he refused and said to his master's wife, "You see, my master does not know what goes on in the house, and he has entrusted everything he owns into my hand.
verses.9: I am not greater in this house than he is. He has not withheld anything from me except you, his wife. How then could I do this great wickedness and sin against God?"
verses.10: But she continued to speak to him day after day, and he would not listen to her to lie with her or be with her.
verses.11: One day, when Joseph went into the house to do his duties and there was no one else in the house,
verses.12: she caught him by his garment and said, "Lie with me." But he left his garment in her hand and ran out and went outside.
verses.13: When she saw that he had left his garment in her hand and had fled outside,
verses.14: she called to the household men and said to them, "Bring the Hebrew man in here—he has come to me to lie with me. I raised my voice in a loud cry.
verses.15: When I raised my voice and cried out, he left his garment with me and fled outside and went out."
verses.16: She left his garment with her until his master came home.
verses.17: Then she told him these words, saying, "The Hebrew servant you brought to us tried to mock me.
verses.18: When I raised my voice and cried out, he left his garment with me and fled outside."
verses.19: When his master heard the words his wife spoke to him, saying, "This is what your servant did to me," his anger burned.
verses.20: So the master of Joseph took him and put him into the prison, the place where the king's prisoners were kept. And Joseph remained there in the prison.
verses.21: But the LORD was with Joseph and showed him steadfast love. He gave him favor in the eyes of the chief jailer.
verses.22: The chief jailer put Joseph in charge of all the prisoners who were in the jail, and whatever was done there, Joseph did it.
verses.23: The chief jailer did not concern himself with anything under Joseph's hand, for the LORD was with him and whatever he did, the LORD made it prosper.

notes:
Notes
- v. 8: "You see, my master does not know what goes on in the house" — "You see" is added for clarity, reflecting the Hebrew "הֵן" (hen), which introduces a clarifying statement.
- v. 9: "He has not withheld anything from me except you, his wife" — The Hebrew is literal ("לֹא־חָשַׂךְ מִמֶּנִּי מְאוּמָה כִּי אִם־אוֹתָךְ בַּאֲשֶׁר אַתְּ־אִשְׁתּוֹ"). "Mao'um" is a rare word meaning "anything," so the phrase is "not withheld anything from me except you."
- v. 13: "When she saw that he had left his garment in her hand and had fled outside" — The Hebrew uses a passive construction ("וַיְהִי כִּרְאוֹתָהּ כִּֽי־עָזַב בִּגְדוֹ בְּיָדָהּ וַיָּנָס הַחֽוּצָה") which is rendered in active voice for natural English flow.
- v. 23: "The chief jailer did not concern himself with anything under Joseph's hand" — The Hebrew is "אֵין שַׂר בֵּית־הַסֹּהַר רֹאֶה אֶת־כָּל־מְאוּמָה בְּיָדוֹ". "Mao'um" again is used, meaning "anything," and the phrase is translated to reflect the idea that the jailer did not oversee anything Joseph handled.
raw:
[1] Joseph was taken down to Egypt and sold there by the Ishmaelites to Potiphar, an Egyptian official who was Pharaoh's cupbearer.

[2] The LORD was with Joseph, so that he became a successful man. He was in the household of his Egyptian master,

[3] and his master saw that the LORD was with him and that the LORD made everything he did prosper.

[4] Joseph found favor in his eyes, and he made him a servant in his household. Potiphar put him in charge of his house and gave him everything he owned into his hand.

[5] From the time he put him in charge of his house and all his property, the LORD blessed the Egyptian's household for Joseph's sake. The blessing of the LORD was upon everything he had in the house and in the field.

[6] Potiphar left everything he had in Joseph's charge and did not concern himself with anything except the food he ate. Now Joseph was handsome in appearance and pleasing in form.

[7] After these events, his master's wife set her eyes on Joseph and said, "Lie with me."

[8] But he refused and said to his master's wife, "You see, my master does not know what goes on in the house, and he has entrusted everything he owns into my hand.

[9] I am not greater in this house than he is. He has not withheld anything from me except you, his wife. How then could I do this great wickedness and sin against God?"

[10] But she continued to speak to him day after day, and he would not listen to her to lie with her or be with her.

[11] One day, when Joseph went into the house to do his duties and there was no one else in the house,

[12] she caught him by his garment and said, "Lie with me." But he left his garment in her hand and ran out and went outside.

[13] When she saw that he had left his garment in her hand and had fled outside,

[14] she called to the household men and said to them, "Bring the Hebrew man in here—he has come to me to lie with me. I raised my voice in a loud cry.

[15] When I raised my voice and cried out, he left his garment with me and fled outside and went out."

[16] She left his garment with her until his master came home.

[17] Then she told him these words, saying, "The Hebrew servant you brought to us tried to mock me.

[18] When I raised my voice and cried out, he left his garment with me and fled outside."

[19] When his master heard the words his wife spoke to him, saying, "This is what your servant did to me," his anger burned.

[20] So the master of Joseph took him and put him into the prison, the place where the king's prisoners were kept. And Joseph remained there in the prison.

[21] But the LORD was with Joseph and showed him steadfast love. He gave him favor in the eyes of the chief jailer.

[22] The chief jailer put Joseph in charge of all the prisoners who were in the jail, and whatever was done there, Joseph did it.

[23] The chief jailer did not concern himself with anything under Joseph's hand, for the LORD was with him and whatever he did, the LORD made it prosper.
